item.title: Free Pet Food Giveaway Today at PJ's Coffee; Salzman Hosts Storm Recovery Event
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: State Representative Michelle Salzman is hosting a free pet food distribution today from 11 a.m. to 1 p.m. at PJ's Coffee, 85 W Airport Blvd in Pensacola, aimed at helping local families still recovering from Hurricane Isaias. The event, sponsored by the Walmart Foundation and organized in partnership with Jennifer Harrison, will provide both dog…
item.content:encoded:
State Representative Michelle Salzman is hosting a free pet food distribution today from 11 a.m. to 1 p.m. at PJ's Coffee, 85 W Airport Blvd in Pensacola, aimed at helping local families still recovering from Hurricane Isaias.

The event, sponsored by the Walmart Foundation and organized in partnership with Jennifer Harrison, will provide both dog and cat food to pet owners facing added expenses during storm recovery. Salzman said the distribution recognizes that pets are an important part of households and that ensuring they're fed is part of easing the broader burden families face after a hurricane. "By working together, we can help ensure that families and their pets have the support they need as we continue moving forward," she said in a statement.

PJ's Coffee is providing the venue at no cost and will offer free hot or iced coffee to everyone who attends. Salzman also noted that residents can contact their local animal shelter, which is offering additional pet assistance programs for those seeking help during the recovery period.

item.title: DeSantis Unveils Christopher Columbus Statue in Naples
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Governor Ron DeSantis unveiled a statue of Christopher Columbus in Naples on Wednesday as part of Florida's America250 initiative marking the nation's 250th anniversary. The Italian explorer's likeness was installed in a city that shares its name with the Italian metropolitan area, creating what state officials say is a fitting connection to…
item.content:encoded:
Governor Ron DeSantis unveiled a statue of Christopher Columbus in Naples on Wednesday as part of Florida's America250 initiative marking the nation's 250th anniversary. The Italian explorer's likeness was installed in a city that shares its name with the Italian metropolitan area, creating what state officials say is a fitting connection to Columbus's heritage.

The statue commemorates Columbus's voyages beginning in 1492, which opened transatlantic exploration and eventually led to European settlement of the Americas, including Florida. State officials noted that Columbus's expeditions inspired subsequent explorers who shaped early Florida, including Juan Ponce de León and Pedro Menéndez de Avilés, who founded St. Augustine in 1565.

"Columbus remains an important figure in Italian-American heritage and a prominent part of the history of Western exploration," the Governor's office said in a statement. Michele Mistò, Consul General of Italy in Miami, called the unveiling an important recognition during Italian-American Heritage Month, noting Italy's ongoing contributions to Florida's economy and culture.

The Naples monument is part of DeSantis's broader effort to preserve American history through the America250 initiative. In February 2025, the Governor announced plans to install additional statues honoring the Founding Fathers, including George Washington, Thomas Jefferson, Benjamin Franklin, James Madison, James Monroe, and Alexander Hamilton.

item.content:encoded:

The cancellation reflects the city's resource allocation priorities in the weeks following hurricane impact. The board typically handles matters related to city parks, recreation programming, and facilities management.

item.title: Jack Brewer Foundation distributes 1,000 free meals in Milton today
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The Jack Brewer Foundation is back at Jernigan's Landing in Milton today with free prepared meals for residents still recovering from Hurricane Isaias. The distribution runs at noon and 6 p.m., with 1,000 meals available on a first-come, first-served basis — up to four per vehicle. The City of Milton has set up a traffic route to keep things…
item.content:encoded:
The Jack Brewer Foundation is back at Jernigan's Landing in Milton today with free prepared meals for residents still recovering from Hurricane Isaias. The distribution runs at noon and 6 p.m., with 1,000 meals available on a first-come, first-served basis — up to four per vehicle.

The City of Milton has set up a traffic route to keep things moving: drivers enter from Canal Street, turn left onto Pine Street, then left onto South Willing Street for pickup. After grabbing meals, head right onto Elmira Street and exit via Oak Street.

If you or someone you know needs a meal, head out to Jernigan's Landing today. The foundation has been a steady presence in the community's hurricane recovery effort.

item.title: Milton lifts boil water advisory after Hurricane Isaias recovery
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The City of Milton announced Thursday that it has lifted a precautionary boil water advisory that was in effect for all city water customers following Hurricane Isaias. The advisory is no longer necessary after water services were restored and required water quality testing confirmed the system is safe for normal use, according to a city news…
item.content:encoded: The City of Milton announced Thursday that it has lifted a precautionary boil water advisory that was in effect for all city water customers following Hurricane Isaias. The advisory is no longer necessary after water services were restored and required water quality testing confirmed the system is safe for normal use, according to a city news release. Residents no longer need to boil water before drinking, cooking, brushing teeth, or other household activities. The precautionary measure had been issued due to storm-related disruptions to the city's water system and concerns about potential contamination from reduced water pressure during the hurricane's aftermath. The City of Milton thanked utility crews, emergency responders, and residents for their patience during the restoration process. Residents with questions about water services can contact the city at (850) 983-5400.

item.title: Milton extends emergency declaration through Oct. 18 after Hurricane Isaias
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The City of Milton has extended its local state of emergency through Sunday, October 18, following Hurricane Isaias, according to a city news release issued today. Mayor Heather Lindsay signed Resolution No. 2026-22, extending the emergency declaration that was originally issued on October 8. The extension allows Milton to continue using emergency…
item.content:encoded:
The City of Milton has extended its local state of emergency through Sunday, October 18, following Hurricane Isaias, according to a city news release issued today. Mayor Heather Lindsay signed Resolution No. 2026-22, extending the emergency declaration that was originally issued on October 8.

The extension allows Milton to continue using emergency powers to protect public health, safety, and welfare. Those powers include expediting emergency contracts, securing equipment and supplies, deploying personnel and volunteers, and reallocating resources to support ongoing response and recovery operations.

City officials noted that the extension does not impose new restrictions on residents or issue additional evacuation orders. The city says it remains focused on protecting public safety, restoring essential services, and supporting residents affected by the hurricane.

item.title: Santa Rosa County warns of contractor scams after storms
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Santa Rosa County Building Inspections is alerting residents to be on guard against unlicensed contractors and scammers seeking to exploit homeowners dealing with storm damage repairs. Following major storms, con artists and unqualified workers often target property owners trying to fix damage quickly. The county is urging residents to take…
item.content:encoded:
Santa Rosa County Building Inspections is alerting residents to be on guard against unlicensed contractors and scammers seeking to exploit homeowners dealing with storm damage repairs.

Following major storms, con artists and unqualified workers often target property owners trying to fix damage quickly. The county is urging residents to take precautions before hiring anyone for repairs, including roofing, electrical, or structural work.

Key steps to protect yourself: verify any contractor's license through the Florida Department of Business and Professional Regulation at MyFloridaLicense.com; avoid door-to-door solicitations or pressure to make quick decisions; never pay the full project cost upfront, especially in cash; get all work details in writing with a contract covering scope, materials, cost, payment schedule, and completion date; and confirm whether permits are required—many storm repairs do need them.

Red flags to watch for include contractors who won't provide license information, discourage permits or inspections, or ask you to pull a permit as an owner-builder when they'll actually do the work. Santa Rosa County Building Inspections can answer questions at (850) 981-7000 before you hire. To report suspected unlicensed contracting, contact the Florida Department of Business and Professional Regulation online.

item.title: Pensacola Police, FDLE Expand Investigation Into Arrested Officer Matthew Baxter
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: PENSACOLA, Fla. — Investigators are examining whether alleged criminal conduct involving a part-time Pensacola police officer extended beyond the incident that led to his arrest on felony narcotics charges. Matthew Baxter was arrested following an investigation conducted by the Pensacola Police Department and the Florida Department of Law…
item.content:encoded:
PENSACOLA, Fla. — Investigators are examining whether alleged criminal conduct involving a part-time Pensacola police officer extended beyond the incident that led to his arrest on felony narcotics charges.


Matthew Baxter was arrested following an investigation conducted by the Pensacola Police Department and the Florida Department of Law Enforcement.

The investigation involved allegations that Baxter purchased oxycodone while wearing his police uniform and driving a department vehicle after completing a shift at Pensacola International Airport.


During an interview Thursday morning on NewsRadio 92.3's Pensacola's Morning News, Pensacola Police spokesman Mike Wood said investigators are looking into Baxter's past conduct.


"We are cooperating with FDLE," Wood said. "They're going to look back and see how far back it goes and see exactly what else is going on with that individual."

Wood emphasized that the department intends to cooperate fully with the investigation.

He also rejected the suggestion that officers would protect a colleague accused of criminal activity.


"None of our careers, our integrity, our pensions, none of that is worth trying to cover for a bad cop," Wood said.


The investigation remains ongoing.


Authorities have not announced whether additional charges will be filed or whether investigators have identified other incidents involving Baxter.

Baxter's charges are allegations, and he is presumed innocent unless proven guilty.

item.title: Pensacola Police Report Isolated Thefts, No Widespread Looting Following Hurricane Isaias
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: PENSACOLA, Fla. — Despite widespread hurricane damage, extended power outages and neighborhoods filled with debris, Pensacola Police say the city has not experienced widespread looting following Hurricane Isaias. That doesn't mean there haven't been some unusual thefts. During an interview Thursday morning on NewsRadio 92.3's Pensacola's Morning…
item.content:encoded:
PENSACOLA, Fla. — Despite widespread hurricane damage, extended power outages and neighborhoods filled with debris, Pensacola Police say the city has not experienced widespread looting following Hurricane Isaias.


That doesn't mean there haven't been some unusual thefts.


During an interview Thursday morning on NewsRadio 92.3's Pensacola's Morning News, department spokesman Mike Wood said officers have made arrests involving the theft of copper from downed utility lines.


Police also arrested someone accused of stealing a stop sign.


"We've made arrests of people already taking lines that are down — the copper," Wood said. "And we had an individual stealing a stop sign. Why? I don't know, but we've made arrests for both of those so far."


Wood said the department has investigated some burglaries but has not seen the widespread looting sometimes feared following major disasters.


"We've had a couple of burglaries and again, those thefts, but as far as a lot of looting at one time everywhere, we did not see that," Wood said.


Hurricane Isaias left extensive damage throughout Pensacola, including downed trees, damaged utility infrastructure and widespread power outages.


Police continue monitoring neighborhoods and responding to calls as residents and businesses work through the recovery process.

item.title: NAS Pensacola Resumes Normal Operations; Naval Aviation Museum and Lighthouse Reopen
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: PENSACOLA, Fla. — Naval Air Station Pensacola is returning to normal operations Thursday, October 15, following Hurricane Isaias. The installation announced Wednesday that operations would resume five days after the Category 2 hurricane struck the Florida Gulf Coast. The reopening includes two of Pensacola's most recognizable attractions. The…
item.content:encoded:
PENSACOLA, Fla. — Naval Air Station Pensacola is returning to normal operations Thursday, October 15, following Hurricane Isaias.


The installation announced Wednesday that operations would resume five days after the Category 2 hurricane struck the Florida Gulf Coast.


The reopening includes two of Pensacola's most recognizable attractions.


The National Naval Aviation Museum and Pensacola Lighthouse are reopening to visitors who do not possess military identification.


Public visitors can access the attractions through the installation's West Gate between 9 a.m. and 3 p.m.


Some recreational facilities remain closed because of storm-related impacts.


NAS Pensacola says the Morale, Welfare and Recreation-operated A.C. Read Golf Course and installation marinas will remain closed until further notice.

The reopening is another sign of progress as military installations, businesses and public facilities across Northwest Florida return to normal operations.


Residents and visitors should continue checking official installation announcements for changes to access requirements and facility availability.

This is routine testing conducted by the base, though it can affect recreational and commercial boating traffic in the region. Anyone with questions about the testing or specific boundary information can contact Eglin Air Force Base public affairs.

item.title: IRS Extends Federal Tax Deadlines for Hurricane Isaias Victims in Northwest Florida
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: PENSACOLA, Fla. — Residents and businesses across Northwest Florida affected by Hurricane Isaias are receiving additional time to meet certain federal tax deadlines. The Internal Revenue Service announced Wednesday that qualifying taxpayers in Escambia, Santa Rosa, Okaloosa, Walton and numerous other Florida counties now have until February 8,…
item.content:encoded:
PENSACOLA, Fla. — Residents and businesses across Northwest Florida affected by Hurricane Isaias are receiving additional time to meet certain federal tax deadlines.


The Internal Revenue Service announced Wednesday that qualifying taxpayers in Escambia, Santa Rosa, Okaloosa, Walton and numerous other Florida counties now have until February 8, 2027, to file certain federal tax returns and make qualifying payments.

The relief generally applies to deadlines falling on or after October 9, 2026, and before February 8, 2027.


That includes certain individual and business income-tax returns, estimated tax payments and employment-related filings.


The IRS says eligible taxpayers with addresses in the covered disaster area will generally receive the relief automatically.


Taxpayers who qualify because their necessary records are located in the disaster area, but who live elsewhere, may need to contact the agency.


There is an important distinction for taxpayers who previously requested an extension to file their 2025 federal income-tax returns.


While the filing deadline may be postponed, tax payments originally due April 15, 2026, are not covered by the new extension.


The IRS also announced limited penalty relief for certain payroll and excise tax deposits.

Residents and businesses should review the agency's official announcement to determine which deadlines apply to their circumstances.


The IRS says additional disaster-related tax relief may become available as recovery continues.

item.title: Santa Rosa County Reports More Than 2,000 Structures Damaged by Hurricane Isaias
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: MILTON, Fla. — The number of structures affected by Hurricane Isaias in Santa Rosa County has surpassed 2,000 as damage-assessment teams continue documenting the storm's destruction. According to the county's Wednesday evening update, more than 80 structures have been classified as destroyed. Approximately 300 sustained major damage, while more…
item.content:encoded:
MILTON, Fla. — The number of structures affected by Hurricane Isaias in Santa Rosa County has surpassed 2,000 as damage-assessment teams continue documenting the storm's destruction.


According to the county's Wednesday evening update, more than 80 structures have been classified as destroyed.


Approximately 300 sustained major damage, while more than 600 were classified as having minor damage.


Officials say more than 2,000 structures have been affected overall, and assessments are continuing.


The hurricane also left an enormous debris-removal operation ahead.

Santa Rosa County now estimates approximately 1.5 million cubic yards of storm debris will need to be removed.


The estimated cost of that operation is $23 million.


The county began its first pass of storm-debris collection Wednesday, with multiple collection passes planned.


Residents should place eligible storm debris along public rights-of-way, keeping vegetation separate from construction and demolition material.


County officials are also asking property owners to report hurricane damage through the Santa Rosa County Property Appraiser's website.


Residents can search for their property and select the damage-reporting option.

Those reports will help document losses as officials pursue additional state and federal disaster assistance.


The county's damage figures remain preliminary and could change as assessments continue.

item.title: Escambia County Meets FEMA Public Assistance Threshold; Individual Assistance Still Pending
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: PENSACOLA, Fla. — Escambia County has reached an important milestone in its effort to secure federal assistance following Hurricane Isaias. County officials announced Wednesday that joint damage-assessment teams have determined Escambia meets the threshold for FEMA Public Assistance. That program provides reimbursement for eligible government…
item.content:encoded:
PENSACOLA, Fla. — Escambia County has reached an important milestone in its effort to secure federal assistance following Hurricane Isaias.


County officials announced Wednesday that joint damage-assessment teams have determined Escambia meets the threshold for FEMA Public Assistance.


That program provides reimbursement for eligible government expenses associated with disaster response and recovery.


Those expenses can include debris removal, emergency protective measures and repairs to damaged public infrastructure.


However, the county's announcement does not mean federal assistance has been approved for individual homeowners.


FEMA Individual Assistance is a separate program that can provide eligible households with assistance for disaster-related needs.


County officials said Wednesday evening that assessment teams were continuing to document residential damage throughout Escambia County and the City of Pensacola.

Once the assessments are complete, the information will be forwarded to the state to support a request for a presidential major disaster declaration.


Both Public Assistance and Individual Assistance require the appropriate federal declaration before funding can move forward.


Escambia County previously estimated approximately $64 million in public damage and recovery costs following Hurricane Isaias.


Pensacola Mayor D.C. Reeves also reported that more than $70 million in private-property damage had been documented within the city as of Tuesday evening.


Those figures represent different categories of damage and should not be confused with approved federal reimbursement amounts.

County officials are encouraging residents to continue reporting hurricane damage through the county's official damage-reporting system.


Reporting damage helps document the community's losses but is not the same as applying for FEMA assistance.
